newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen nearing bottom - Merrill.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen nearing bottom - Merrill.

text.p: Thai stocks are nearing the bottom of a bear run and might be able to climb by the end of this year, Merrill Lynch said in a report on Monday.
"Intermediate term uncertainties in each sector has tempered the boldness of analysts recommendations. We believe this is the classic case of a tail end of a bear market," it said.

Hit by a range of economic concerns The Stock Exchange of Thailand's composite SET Index has fallen by 41 percent over the last 12 months to stand at 703.32 by the close on Monday against 1189 in March last year.

Last week the authorities ordered a sweeping shake up of the troubled finance sector where high loan exposure by financial institutions to the depressed property sector has been viewed negatively by markets and investors.
Ten weakened finance companies were told to raise capital and banks and finance companies were asked to raise provisions for poor quality loans.
But Merrill said values had appeared in many areas of the market.
"We believe the historic price earnings and price to book ratio are touching very attractive levels not seen for many years," it added.
Thai lenders could cope with problem loans and Merrill believes the market could rise to over 1000 by the end of 1997.

"Even if the SET suffers a one-off 20-25 percent earnings per share contraction because of loans write-offs, the market should be able to recover to 1000 by end-1997 so long as the economic cycle is going in the right direction," the report added.
Loan portfolio quality may yet deteriorate further but selected bank stocks have become attractive buys, Merrill said.
"Non-performing loans will likely take another two years to peak. Banks are unlikely to register strong earnings growth soon - our forecast is 10-11 percent in 1997 for the top 10 banks," it said.
Merill recommends Bangkok Bank Plc Thai Farmers Bank Plc and First Bangkok City Bank Plc.
National Finance and Securities and Asia Credit Plc were the firm's recommendations among finance stocks.
"Most finance stocks have likely discounted all the possible bad news. It is not widely appreciated that the top financial companies are better capitalised than the banks," the report said.
But Merrill warned that only the fittest property companies would emerge from a prolonged downturn in the local real estate market.
"In our opinion only the fittest will survive the current slump. We recommend investrors stick with premium names like Land and House Plc," it said.

Merrill places a neutral recommendation on the energy sector which it believed had acted as a haven for investors seeking refuge from problems plaguing the broader market but believed PTTEP Plc offered long term potential.
"A recent sharp correction has taken the froth off PTTEP and we believe it offers long term value now," said the firm.
PTTEP is the exploration and invstment of state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand.
Uncertainty surrounding telecoms stocks would continue and cloud opportunities in the sector, the report said.

"While many Thai telecom holding companies trade at discounts, their core trading businesses appear to be showing a material deterioration. Consequently we do not recommend any telecom stocks in the intermediate terms," the report said.
